movement_source: row 'Net profit excluding Notable Items', column FY24 (Sep 2024) -> column FY25 (Sep 2025)
headline: Westpac's cash earnings (net profit excluding Notable Items) fell $141 million (-2%) to $6,972 million in FY25 from $7,113 million in FY24. Total operating income grew 3% to $22,464 million, driven by a 3% rise in net interest income to $19,473 million and a 5% increase in non-interest income to $2,991 million. However, pre-provision profit declined 3% to $10,548 million as underlying operating expenses rose 6% (excluding restructuring charges). A $113 million reduction in credit impairment charges was more than offset by the expense growth. Statutory profit was $6,916 million.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $557 million (+3%) to $19,473 million. The bank attributes this to volume growth, partially offset by a 1 bps margin decline to 1.94%. Core NII also rose 3% to $18,191 million.
Non-interest income rose $144 million (+5%) to $2,991 million. Net fees contributed $60 million of growth, up 4% to $1,732 million.

Underlying operating expenses increased $672 million (+6%). Headline expenses were $11,916 million (+9%), including a $273 million restructuring charge. Staff costs rose 7% to $6,326 million; technology costs rose 13% to $3,136 million.
Credit impairment charges decreased by $113 million (-21%) to $424 million, providing a positive contribution to earnings compared to the prior year's $537 million charge.

Tax expense decreased slightly by $34 million (-1%) to $3,135 million on a statutory basis. On an ex-notable basis, tax expense moved from $3,169 million to $3,135 million (a decrease of $34 million), contributing positively to the bottom line despite a slight increase in the effective tax rate.
Notable items reduced profit by $56 million in FY25, compared to a $123 million reduction in FY24. This represents a $67 million positive swing in the drag from notable items year-on-year.

notable_items: Hedging/IFRS volatility adjustments (statutory vs cash reconciliation)
limitations: The residual of -$16 million is unexplained, likely due to rounding differences between the headline ex-notable profit and the sum of the statutory components adjusted for notable items.
Tax impact calculated using statutory tax expense delta as a proxy for the ex-notable tax movement.

Capped at 80: nii +557 $m, other_operating_income +144 $m, operating_expenses -672 $m, credit_impairment_charge +113 $m, notable_items +67 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
Failed check: drivers_reconcile (drivers +233.0 + residual -16.0 != delta -141.0, tol 1.0)
